purpose: Fictional adaptive pre-review tests only. Not FN example answers, participant evidence or target readiness levels.

personas.background: A fictional resident answering personally, unfamiliar with drones before this conversation.
unknown_facts: What a drone is before the interview
Healthcare drone deliveries before the interview
Whether any local drone service exists
benefits_perceived: Urgent medical deliveries might help people if reliable
information_needs: Measurements compared with existing road deliveries
Who is responsible if problems occur
personas.communication_style: Plain short answers; express uncertainty where facts are unknown
behavioural_traits: Accept the short explanation and continue when offered
Only raise relevant concerns when asked
No participation opportunity has been offered
Could compare evidence and make a suggestion if given an accessible opportunity
personas.contradiction_policy: Correct accidental inconsistencies without inventing experiences
expected_observations: Prior unfamiliarity remains distinct from supplied information
Wildlife is admitted without requiring an indicator match
No opportunity is not inability or demonstrated influence
prohibited_inferences: A numeric readiness level from unfamiliarity

personas.background: A fictional resident who knows general drone uses and once attended a fictional online consultation about a proposed healthcare delivery service.
known_facts: A drone is an aircraft without an onboard pilot
Photography, inspections and deliveries are possible uses
Healthcare deliveries can include medicines and samples
unknown_facts: Whether the proposed service now operates
Whether consultation feedback changed the route
actual_experiences: Attended one online consultation in this fictional scenario
actual_participation: Asked about night flights and accessibility during that consultation
actual_contributions: Suggested avoiding night flights and providing a non-digital feedback channel
reported_outcomes: Received an acknowledgement, with no confirmed change in the decision
benefits_perceived: Faster urgent deliveries may help remote patients
concerns: Unequal access to the service and consultation
conditions: Offer accessible consultation and a response to complaints
information_needs: Who benefits and who bears impacts
personas.communication_style: Give a relevant concrete example, then state its limits
behavioural_traits: Distinguish submitting an opinion from demonstrated influence
Would continue monitoring if accessible information were published
personas.contradiction_policy: Correct accidental inconsistencies without inventing outcomes
expected_observations: Extended participation and influence probes remain distinct
An acknowledgement is not a demonstrated policy change
Priority topics are reused for evidence and accountability

personas.background: A fictional hospital logistics planning unit. Its remit covers proposed delivery requirements, internal coordination and staff preparation. It does not regulate airspace, certify aircraft or authorise drone operators.
known_facts: Draft requirements cover secure handover and delivery reliability
A draft pilot plan exists but has not been formally adopted
Staff time and a pilot budget have been requested but not allocated
unknown_facts: Whether requested resources will be approved
actual_experiences: Internal planning discussions and a draft risk register
actual_participation: Planning staff helped draft proposed requirements
actual_contributions: Proposed secure handover and incident escalation arrangements
reported_outcomes: Drafts remain under review; no formal adoption
personas.communication_style: Distinguish a proposal from an existing arrangement and state remit limits
behavioural_traits: No drone pilot has been tested by this unit
personas.contradiction_policy: Do not promote drafts into adopted or tested arrangements
expected_observations: Assessment stays within the unit's remit
Draft plans, requested resources, testing and integration are distinguished

personas.background: A fictional researcher assessing only a reusable temperature-controlled sample container, configuration v0.3, intended for integration with a healthcare drone. Expertise covers container thermal tests and the mounting interface, not the aircraft or complete delivery system.
known_facts: Bench tests in a temperature chamber used configuration v0.3 and simulated payloads
The sensor logs showed the specified thermal range was maintained during those controlled tests
The mounting interface has only a bench mock-up
actual_experiences: Controlled temperature-chamber tests on this component configuration
actual_participation: Designed and ran component thermal experiments
actual_contributions: Recorded sensor logs and identified mounting-interface limitations
reported_outcomes: Controlled thermal results only; no flight, representative-environment or operational demonstration
personas.acceptance_position: promising component with substantial validation remaining
personas.communication_style: Name the exact configuration, test environment and limitations; avoid invented measurements
personas.uncertainty_tolerance: explicit about untested environments and interfaces
behavioural_traits: Never transfer component evidence to the whole drone system
Do not invent numerical temperatures, durations or test counts
No qualification or repeated operational use has been demonstrated
expected_observations: Assessed object remains the v0.3 container component
Controlled tests are not representative or operational demonstration
Component evidence is not whole-system maturity
